claims.claim: The World Food Programme is ending monthly support for more than half a million people in Gaza after aid cuts, according to its director for Palestine, who said winter is likely to deepen hunger.
claims.episode_span: ending food support for more than half a million people each month
claims.source_title: Cuts force World Food Programme to end support for half a million Palestinians in Gaza
claims.supporting_quote: This winter is likely to deepen hunger for Palestinians in Gaza, after sweeping aid cuts forced the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) to end support for more than half a million people each month, the agency’s director for Palestine said.

claims.claim: Two-thirds of Gaza’s population face crisis levels of food insecurity and 200,000 people are in danger of famine, The Guardian reports.
claims.episode_span: two-thirds of the population face crisis levels of food insecurity
claims.source_title: Cuts force World Food Programme to end support for half a million Palestinians in Gaza
claims.supporting_quote: Two-thirds of population face crisis levels of food insecurity and 200,000 people are in danger of famine

claims.claim: More than a year after a Trump-brokered ceasefire, promised reconstruction in Gaza has not begun, there are few jobs, and the vast majority still rely on aid.
claims.source_title: Cuts force World Food Programme to end support for half a million Palestinians in Gaza
claims.supporting_quote: More than a year after a Trump-brokered ceasefire came into force, promised reconstruction has not begun, there are few jobs and the vast majority in Gaza still rely on aid to eat.

claims.claim: China’s GDP grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, better than economists expected and up from 4.3 percent in the second quarter.
claims.episode_span: grew 4.5 percent year on year between July and September
claims.source_title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
claims.supporting_quote: China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.

claims.claim: Roaring exports lifted China’s third-quarter growth, factory output grew much faster than consumer spending, and electronics demand buoyed industrial output amid an AI boom.
claims.episode_span: Roaring exports lifted growth in the quarter
claims.source_title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
claims.supporting_quote: Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.

claims.claim: Laurent Nunez admitted police lost control in some cities, cited a lack of anticipation, and tendered a resignation Macron did not accept.
claims.episode_span: the police “lost control” in some cities
claims.source_title: French interior minister admits police 'lost control' of protests
claims.supporting_quote: France's Interior Minister Laurent Nunez admitted Monday that the police "lost control" in some cities during violent protests that erupted in cities across the country at the weekend. He said there had been a "lack of anticipation" in preparations and that he had tendered his resignation to President Emmanuel Macron "because I felt responsible for everything that happened." Macron did not accept his resignation.

claims.claim: Macron held an emergency meeting Sunday and warned that those who looted will have to pay, after shopfronts were demolished and stock worth thousands of euros was stolen.
claims.episode_span: those who looted will have to pay for the damage
claims.source_title: French shops demolished after weekend riots across the country
claims.supporting_quote: On Sunday, President Macron held an emergency meeting with senior government officials, warning that "those who looted will have to pay for the damage".

claims.claim: The Guardian reports 2,400 arrests in France, yellow-vest demonstrations called for October 24 and November 5, and a Meloni security meeting Monday after looting in Milan.
claims.source_title: France braces for weeks more of protests as unrest spreads to Italy – Europe live
claims.supporting_quote: There are no signs of French protests stopping anytime soon: the yellow vest movement, de gilets jaunes , has just announced a “second act” of protests for upcoming Saturday, 24 October – and then again a week after that, too.

claims.claim: Texas early voting runs Monday through October 30 under maps passed after Trump said Republicans were entitled to five more seats.
claims.episode_span: early voting in Texas kicks off Monday and runs through October 30
claims.source_title: Texans head to the polls, putting Trump’s redistricting map to the test
claims.supporting_quote: Early voting in the Lone Star State kicks off Monday and runs through Oct. 30.

claims.claim: Republican officials in Tarrant County cut Election Day voting locations by 30 percent, and thousands of Texans were affected by a registration backlog.
claims.episode_span: slashed Election Day voting locations by 30 percent
claims.source_title: Texans head to the polls, putting Trump’s redistricting map to the test
claims.supporting_quote: Voters in Tarrant County, a major battleground area, are preparing for the possibility of longer lines at the polls after Republican local officials slashed Election Day voting locations by 30%.

claims.claim: Mail ballots in Texas must be returned by 7 p.m. on Election Day or by 5 p.m. the next day if postmarked by Election Day, and Robert Howden became secretary of state in July.
claims.episode_span: mail ballots must be returned by 7 p.m. on Election Day
claims.source_title: Texans head to the polls, putting Trump’s redistricting map to the test
claims.supporting_quote: In Texas, mail ballots must be returned by 7 p.m. on Election Day, or by 5 p.m. the following day as long as the envelope is postmarked by Election Day.

claims.claim: The Wall Street Journal, as cited by Voice of Emirates, reported a Kremlin proposal for a Trump-Putin-Xi summit beside APEC in Shenzhen from November 8 to 19 that would exclude Zelensky.
claims.source_title: Trump is open to a trilateral summit with Putin and Xi Jinping without Zelensky’s participation
claims.supporting_quote: According to these sources, the Russian initiative suggests holding the proposed summit on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, which is scheduled to take place in the Chinese city of Shenzhen between November 8 and 19.

claims.claim: Trump said things were going very well but did not confirm the summit; a US official said he has not given final approval but appears open; Peskov said there is no concrete plan.
claims.episode_span: there is, as of now, no concrete plan and no clear agenda
claims.source_title: Trump is open to a trilateral summit with Putin and Xi Jinping without Zelensky’s participation
claims.supporting_quote: Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for the Russian presidency (the Kremlin), confirmed that discussions and consultations are underway regarding the possibility of holding this significant meeting. However, he clarified that, as of now, there is no concrete plan or clear agenda for the meeting.

claims.claim: Leaks attributed to a former Russian intelligence officer say Putin raised the summit on an October 9 call that also included a preliminary understanding on US purchases of Russian diesel.
claims.episode_span: a direct phone call with Trump on October 9
claims.source_title: Trump is open to a trilateral summit with Putin and Xi Jinping without Zelensky’s participation
claims.supporting_quote: Additional leaks, cited by media outlets and attributed to a former Russian intelligence officer, reveal that the proposal for a trilateral summit was put forward by President Putin during a direct phone call with Trump on October 9th.

claims.claim: Qatar’s deputy prime minister warned energy shockwaves from the Iran war have yet to peak, called for dialogue with Tehran, highlighted US defence ties and rejected Strait of Hormuz transit fees.
claims.episode_span: energy shockwaves have yet to peak
claims.source_title: Qatar warns global energy shockwaves from Iran war have yet to peak
claims.supporting_quote: Deputy PM calls for dialogue with Tehran, highlights US defence ties and rejects Strait of Hormuz transit fees.

claims.claim: Alberta is voting on whether to hold a separation referendum, and the BBC says polling suggests most Albertans favour remaining in Canada.
claims.episode_span: whether to hold a separation vote
claims.source_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada
claims.supporting_quote: Polling suggests most Albertans favour remaining part of the country, although the debate alone has proven divisive.

claims.claim: The Coast Guard halted a search off Mexico after 16 people were rescued, 11 were missing, and three had injuries consistent with shark bites.
claims.episode_span: rescuing sixteen people; eleven are missing
claims.source_title: Coast Guard Halts Search for Survivors of Capsized Boat Off Mexico
claims.supporting_quote: Some 11 people were missing but 16 were rescued, including three who had injuries consistent with shark bites, the authorities said.

claims.claim: A fire at a Canadian military base killed four men, injured dozens, and spread a kilometre in 30 to 60 seconds.
claims.episode_span: killed four men and injured dozens after moving a kilometre
claims.source_title: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
claims.supporting_quote: The blaze that killed four men and injured dozens of others spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.

claims.claim: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, 65, was struck by a car outside her office; a suspect is in custody and the counterterrorism team was activated.
claims.episode_span: Helen Haines, sixty-five, was struck by a car outside her office
claims.source_title: Australian Lawmaker Helen Haines Injured After Attack, Prime Minister Says
claims.supporting_quote: A suspect is in custody and the country’s counterterrorism team was activated after Helen Haines, 65, was struck by a car outside her office.
